title: Pittsburgh medical student Anna Li used a 3D printer to build a stethoscope for home use; her startup Kori
summary: Korion Health 3D printed stethoscope: Discover how Anna Li and Akshaya Anand created Korion Health, winning the Hult Prize and developing a groundbreaking electronic stethoscope for home health monitoring.

contentHtml:
Anna Li wanted to make it easier for people to monitor their heart and lung health without having to visit a hospital. So while working in an emergency department, the University of Pittsburgh MD/PhD student came up with an idea for an electronic stethoscope that patients could use at home. She headed to the university's makerspace, picked up a 3D printer and soldering iron, and started building a prototype.

That early version eventually led to Korion Health, a medical technology company Li co-founded with Akshaya Anand in 2022. The startup went on to win the international Hult Prize, which came with $1 million, and secured an omnibus patent. And by July 2025, it was also working toward US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval.

Anna Li Built Her First Electronic Stethoscope at the University of Pittsburgh

Li developed the first prototype at Benedum Hall's makerspace. She initially hoped to share the design on GitHub, where developers can collaborate on projects, rather than turn it into a business.

Her mentor, however, encouraged her to develop the device further after seeing what she had built, as per a report.

Li eventually teamed up with Anand, a machine-learning graduate student at the University of Maryland. Anand developed the stethoscope's user interface and the two went on to establish Korion Health in 2022, according to a Pittwire report.

The company's idea was to give people without medical training a way to check their heart and lung function at home, potentially reducing unnecessary hospital visits.

Korion Health Won a $1 Million International Hult Prize

The startup even received early support through the University of Pittsburgh's entrepreneurship programmes. Li and Anand finished fourth in the university's Randall Family Big Idea Competition before receiving $25,000 from the Big Idea Center's Advantage Fund.

Korion Health later secured an omnibus patent and won the international Hult Prize, which awarded the company $1 million to continue developing its business, reported Pittwire.

The University of Pittsburgh's July 25, 2025, profile of Li also reported that the company was seeking FDA approval for its electronic stethoscope.

Li told her University's magazine that, “The central thesis of my life has been that I really, really care about people,” adding, “I think the real wealth in life comes from being able to see those you love happy and healthy and to be in a community where people are empowered to live their best lives and take care of each other.”

The Home-Use Stethoscope Uses Augmented Reality to Guide Patients

Korion Health's first prototype combined an affordable, 3D-printed electronic stethoscope with an augmented reality guided interface. The system was designed to teach people without medical training how to use the device for heart and lung screenings.

Li also wanted the product to look different from conventional medical equipment. The updated stethoscope featured a turquoise finish and a rainbow-coloured light. Some of its storage cases came with panda ears and shark fins, adding a playful touch to the device as she told Pittwire, “I’m like, ‘Why can’t medicine be cute? It has to be fun and cute. I will die on this hill.’”

Korion Health Is Still Working Toward FDA Clearance

The company wants to make essential health screenings more accessible through affordable, easy-to-use medical devices. Its SoundHeart stethoscope is central to that effort.

Korion Health's website identifies Li as its CEO and co-founder and Anand as its chief operating officer and co-founder. And the website lists FDA clearance for SoundHeart as a planned 2026 milestone and explicitly states that the product is not yet FDA-cleared.

The startup mentions, "Our product is not yet FDA cleared, and this website is for informational purposes only."
